diagnostic_evidence.quote: The model parameters are $\diffTensor\equiv10^{-3}$, $\velField\equiv0$ ($\peclet_h=0$) in the first row

issues.failure_explanation: For the explicitly considered case b=0, both the denominator ||b||_{L^infty}^2 and div b vanish, producing 0/0. Multiplication by Pe_{H_j}=0 does not define the expression.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the formula for nonzero velocity and add the zero-velocity case, or rewrite the first summand in a continuously defined form such as (H_j/a_min)(||b||_{L^infty}^2+a_min||div b||_{L^infty})^{1/2}.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit quantification of C_j is not defined on the pure-diffusion regime, although the existence statement for the eigenvalue decay itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Quantified eigenvalue constant is undefined for zero velocity
issues.why_classification: A local degenerate-case definition restores the same decay result and all advertised uses, with no new lemma or loss of rate or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying the global estimate by the displayed local stability factor yields C_B(1+C Pe_H), not (1+C Pe_H)^2. For div b=0, C_B contains the domain-scale quantity 1+||b||_infty/a_min, whereas Pe_H contains H_j^*||b||_infty/a_min. As the oversampling size decreases with global data fixed, the asserted dimensionless C does not absorb the missing 1/H_j^* factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bound with the supported prefactor C_B(1+C Pe_H), or with explicit local- and global-Péclet factors, unless a new argument proves that the global convection dependence cancels.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit parameter dependence claimed by the corollary is unsupported; a weaker estimate involving the global operator norm or a domain-scale Péclet number is what the displayed calculation supports.
issues.title: Corollary's stated local-Péclet prefactor is not the prefactor proved
issues.why_classification: The repair weakens the explicit parameter dependence but preserves a comparable convergence estimate and requires no new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The error u^e-u_j^p is harmonic but does not vanish on the artificial boundary ∂Ω_j^*∩Ω. For div b=0, B_{Ω_j^*}(w,w) retains the sign-indefinite trace term -(1/2)∫_{∂Ω_j^*∩Ω} w^2 b·n ds. Thus local coercivity in the a-seminorm is false. For example, on an interior planar subdomain with A=εI, b=(1,0), and w=e^{x_1/ε}, w is B-harmonic, a(w,w)>0, and B(w,w)=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coercivity step with a genuine local particular-solution stability argument, for example by lifting the trace or quotienting out the local a-null constants and using valid Poincaré and outflow-trace estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's local stability estimate is not established, and the proof of the MS-GFEM iteration theorem cannot obtain its required relative approximation bound from this argument.
issues.title: Local coercivity step in the corollary proof is false
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial local stability lemma can preserve a comparable estimate; no entirely new global method or abandonment of the result is required.

issues.failure_explanation: All MS-GFEM corrections lie in the homogeneous Dirichlet ansatz space, so the iteration never changes the trace of u^(k) on Γ_D. If u^e has zero trace but u^(0)∈H^1 has a nonzero trace, the boundary error remains fixed. For pure diffusion with u^e=0 and u^(0)=1, the residual bilinear form vanishes on the homogeneous test space and the iteration makes no update.

failure_location.quote: converges for any initial guess $\fwp^{(0)} \in \Hone$ strictly monotonically

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require u^(0) to lie in H_D^1(Ω), or equivalently require the physical initial guess to satisfy the prescribed Dirichlet trace, and restrict G accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated universal initial-guess guarantee is false; the operator-contraction proof also applies the GFEM error estimate to nonadmissible functions outside the homogeneous solution space.
issues.title: Iteration cannot converge for arbitrary H^1 initial guesses
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard admissible-initial-guess condition preserves the method, rate, and intended scope without a new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Let M_1=Σ_j R_j^Tχ_jB_j^{-1}R_j. The one-level operator is M_1B, so the residual after the half-step is (I-BM_1)r. Hence the hybrid preconditioner consistent with both the continuous formula and the two-step iteration is M_1+R_S^TB_S^{-1}R_S(I-BM_1), not the displayed M_1+R_S^TB_S^{-1}R_S(I-M_1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final factor I-M_1 by I-BM_1 in the displayed preconditioner.
issues.overall_effect: As displayed, M is not the matrix representation of the stated MS-GFEM map, and Richardson iteration with that M is not the subsequent two-level hybrid RAS iteration.
issues.title: Displayed hybrid RAS preconditioner omits a stiffness-matrix factor
issues.why_classification: The local matrix-factor correction is forced by the adjacent two-step construction and restores every stated operation and guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: In the advertised hyperbolic case A≡0, δ_{A n}^-=δ_{A n}^+=0 on every interior face. Both weighted-average formulas and the harmonic-average penalty denominator are therefore 0/0. The source only specifies an auxiliary inner product for the eigenproblem; it does not define the DG discretization in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the zero-diffusion convention, for example w^-=w^+=1/2 and σ_γ=0 when δ_{A n}^-+δ_{A n}^+=0, with all diffusive flux terms omitted.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical procedure used for the vanishing-diffusion experiment is not defined by the stated DG formulas, even though the upwind term itself remains meaningful.
issues.title: Pure-transport DG discretization leaves diffusive weights and penalty undefined
issues.why_classification: A standard local degenerate-case convention makes the advertised hyperbolic computation well-defined without changing the method or its other regimes.

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed field, div b=-80(x_1-0.5)(x_2-0.5)-3. This is sign-changing: it equals 2 at (x_1,x_2)=(0.25,0.75), but -8 at (0.25,0.25). Thus the field is not globally of negative divergence.

failure_location.quote: which has negative divergence and yields an indefinite problem

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'negative divergence' with 'sign-changing divergence' or 'negative divergence on part of the domain'.
issues.overall_effect: The description of the large-scale model's velocity field is false; the claims that it is non-divergence-free and indefinite are not directly invalidated.
issues.title: Large-scale velocity field does not have negative divergence
issues.why_classification: A local wording correction preserves the experiment, its interpretation as an unsupported indefinite test case, and all numerical results.
